issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: new System.ComponentModel.DateOnlyConverter and System.ComponentModel.TimeOnlyConverter classes
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-componentmodel See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation Converting between `System.DateOnly` and `string` is currently not supported using a `System.ComponentModel.TypeConverter`. Many system types are supported out of the box (`System.DateTimeOffset`, `System.Guid`, `System.TimeSpan`, `System.Uri` etc.) so I think `System.DateOnly` would be a welcome addition. I was expecting this to work, but converting from string actually throws: > System.NotSupportedException: TypeConverter cannot convert from System.String. ```csharp TypeConverter dateOnlyConverter = TypeDescriptor.GetConverter(typeof(DateOnly)); DateOnly? date = dateOnlyConverter.ConvertFromString("1940-10-09") as DateOnly?; ``` Having built-in support for type conversion would probably help to drive adoption of the relatively new `DateOnly` type. Addressing this issue would fix #59253 which is mentioned in [System.Runtime work planned for .NET 7](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/64603) (but only under the _Backlog_ list, not the _Planned for .NET 7_ list). Note that a similar proposal for the `System.TimeOnly` type has been filed as #68744. ### API Proposal ```csharp public class DateOnlyConverter : System.ComponentModel.TypeConverter { public override bool CanConvertFrom(System.ComponentModel.ITypeDescriptorContext? context, System.Type sourceType); public override bool CanConvertTo(System.ComponentModel.ITypeDescriptorContext? context, System.Type? destinationType); public override object? ConvertFrom(System.ComponentModel.ITypeDescriptorContext? context, System.Globalization.CultureInfo? culture, object value); public override object? ConvertTo(System.ComponentModel.ITypeDescriptorContext? context, System.Globalization.CultureInfo? culture, object? value, System.Type destinationType); public override bool IsValid(System.ComponentModel.ITypeDescriptorContext? context, object? value); } ``` ### API Usage Using the converter would most likely happen through `TypeDescriptor.GetConverter(typeof(DateOnly))`: ```csharp var dateOnlyConverter = TypeDescriptor.GetConverter(typeof(DateOnly)); var date = dateOnlyConverter.ConvertFromString("1940-10-09") as DateOnly?; ``` or even through a higher level abstractions such as [Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/) (which also uses `TypeDescriptor.GetConverter` internally) as described in #64739: ```csharp // Let's make the end of the world date configurable because we're not really sure about that date var configuration = new ConfigurationBuilder() .AddInMemoryCollection(new Dictionary { ["EndOfWorldDate"] = "2012-12-21" }) .Build(); var endOfTheWorldDate = configuration.GetValue("EndOfWorldDate"); ``` It could also be used by directly creating a `DateOnlyConverter` instance but this is a less likely scenario: ```csharp var dateOnlyConverter = new System.ComponentModel.DateOnlyConverter(); var date = dateOnlyConverter.ConvertFromString("1940-10-09") as DateOnly?; ``` ### Alternative Designs To the best of my knowledge, there's no alternative design that would make sense for adding a new `System.ComponentModel.TypeConverter`. ### Risks `System.ComponentModel.DateOnlyConverter` being a new class, no risks are introduced.

Could you please merge this proposal with the one in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/68744? there is no need to track them in two different proposals. Thanks for filing the proposal.
@thomaslevesque that is right. I believe the ask is to avoid having different users implement the same converters to make their scenarios work.

@0xced I am noticing some differences comparing the proposal to like [DateTimeConverter](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/334989f6cc0600f9c12e9fa989dc1814c8300d1d/src/libraries/System.ComponentModel.TypeConverter/ref/System.ComponentModel.TypeConverter.cs#L354). Any reason for that? you are proposing to have the extra API `IsValid`  (which there is no need to override it) and also you are missing the public constructor and the nullability annotations.
@0xced I have updated the APIs in the proposal. Let's me know if you have any concern.
Thank you for implementing this, Tarek and Jeremy!
